claim: K3s 'Distributed hybrid or multicloud cluster' page (updated 2026-11-09): one cluster may span nodes with no shared private network, but embedded etcd is not supported in that deployment: 'all server nodes must be reachable to each other via their private IPs' and 'all servers should be in the same location'; agents may be distributed over multiple networks; higher latency 'could also impact the health of the cluster if latency is too high'

K3s Tailscale integration (--vpn-auth, experimental since v1.27.3/v1.26.6/v1.25.11) needs a Tailscale auth key that 'can be reusable', pod CIDR routes approved in the coordinator, an ACL rule letting pods talk, and supports a self-hosted control server such as Headscale via controlServerURL; several clusters on one tailnet need distinct pod CIDRs or ACLs

Fleet 0.16 architecture: a 'two-stage pull model' (controller pulls from Git, agents pull from the controller); 'all communication goes from the managed cluster to the Fleet controller'; the controller 'does not initiate connections to downstream clusters' (except optional manager-initiated registration); agents are not assumed to be always connected; the only API is the Kubernetes API

Fleet 0.16 security model: the controller creates a service account per cluster that can only list BundleDeployments in a namespace created for that cluster; the cluster registration token is used only during registration

Fleet 0.16 rolloutStrategy: maxUnavailable (default 100%) per partition, maxUnavailablePartitions (default 0), autoPartitionSize (default 25%), autoPartitionThreshold (default 200 clusters), maxNew (default 50), manual partitions by clusterName/clusterSelector/clusterGroup/clusterGroupSelector processed in order; an offline cluster counts as NotReady; with the default maxUnavailable 100% the partition gate 'is ineffective'; the page describes pausing, not rollback

Fleet 0.16 agent-initiated registration: a ClusterRegistrationToken (with TTL) yields a values file; the fleet-agent Helm chart is installed in the downstream cluster; 'the Manager will never make an outbound API request to the downstream clusters'; the agent forgets the token after registration; since 0.16.3 a registration with an existing client ID but a different token is held pending (RegistrationTokenMismatch event)

Rancher Fleet v0.16.3 (2026-10-23) is the latest non-prerelease; v0.17.0-rc.2 and v0.18.0-alpha.1 are pre-releases (GitHub releases API); release assets include fleet-agent and fleet-controller arm64 binaries and Helm charts

KubeEdge scalability report (2022-07-13, v1.11.0-alpha.0): 'the KubeEdge-powered Kubernetes clusters can stably support 100,000 concurrent edge nodes and more than one million pods' using Edgemark hollow (simulated) nodes and ClusterLoader2 density tests, with one master of 128 CPUs and 256 GB RAM and five CloudCore instances of 12 CPU/48 GB; large-scale disconnection/reconnection, high latency and intermittent links were not yet tested

Open Cluster Management architecture: the klusterlet on each managed cluster 'actively pull[s]' prescriptions from the hub; 'the hub cluster won't directly request against the real clusters' (hub-to-cluster access is an optional reverse-tunnel cluster-proxy add-on); ManifestWork dispatches resources into a per-cluster namespace; Placement selects clusters by labels or cluster-claims; the page claims a hub can 'accept and manage thousands of clusters' without a benchmark

Argo CD keeps managed clusters as Secrets in the Argo CD namespace and the ApplicationSet Cluster generator targets every registered cluster (optionally by label) with the cluster's API server as the destination, i.e. the control plane holds credentials to and connects to each cluster (push)

argocd-agent (argoproj-labs, Apache-2.0, v0.11.0 on 2026-11-11, pre-1.0) adds a hub-and-spoke 'pull model' to Argo CD: 'instead of your control plane reaching out to remote clusters, lightweight agents reach back to a central hub', with certificate-based agent auth and agents that work through intermittent connections

Akri v0.14.0 README: a CNCF Sandbox project that exposes 'heterogeneous leaf devices (such as IP cameras and USB devices) as resources in a Kubernetes cluster', extending the Kubernetes device-plugin framework, continually detecting which nodes can reach which devices and handling 'the dynamic appearance and disappearance of leaf devices'

OpenYurt v1.7.0 README: a CNCF Incubating project built on upstream Kubernetes with 'a centralized Kubernetes control plane residing in the cloud site' managing edge nodes, addressing unreliable or disconnected cloud-edge networking, edge autonomy and region-aware deployment

KubeEdge v1.23.1 README: a CNCF graduated project with a cloud part and an edge part; claims reliable cloud-edge message delivery, 'Edge Autonomy' (edge nodes keep running apps when the cloud link is down or the edge restarts), device management through CRDs and MQTT access for edge devices

Cluster API v1.14.4 README: a Kubernetes SIG Cluster Lifecycle subproject providing 'declarative APIs and tooling to simplify provisioning, upgrading, and operating multiple Kubernetes clusters' through infrastructure, bootstrap and control-plane providers

Rancher Fleet v0.16.3 source, internal/cmd/controller/target/status.go: 'Unavailable for a partition is stricter than unavailable for a target. For a partition a target must be available and up-to-date'; a target is up to date only when its staged, desired and applied deployment IDs all equal the new deployment ID, and a partition is unavailable when its unavailable count exceeds its maxUnavailable. So a target still waiting for a new release counts as unavailable, and maxUnavailable: 0 leaves no room for any target to start updating
